rules.title: Security deposit cap, holding, interest, return, and penalties
rules.requirement: A landlord may require no more than one and one-half months’ rent as security, including prepaid funds such as last month’s rent, and must hold the deposit in trust with required interest notices. After tenancy termination, the landlord generally must return the deposit plus interest within 30 days, less lawful itemized deductions, with shorter return deadlines after certain displacements.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent; return within 30 days; double amount wrongfully withheld

coverage.other_unresolvable: The document states that the investment-account section does not apply to security deposits for seasonal use or rental, defined as a term of not more than 125 consecutive days for residential purposes by a person having a permanent place of residence elsewhere, with exceptions for seasonal, temporary, or migrant farm workers.
coverage.summary: Applies to residential security deposits, with stated special rules depending on whether the landlord receives deposits for ten or fewer units or ten or more units.

rules.exemptions: The document states that the security-deposit investment-account section does not apply to security deposits for seasonal use or rental as defined in N.J.S.A. 46:8-19(d).
rules.penalty: A tenant may sue for double the amount wrongfully withheld plus court costs and reasonable attorney’s fees; willful withholding of deposits involving State or federal assistance may carry a civil penalty of $500 to $2,000 per offense; unlawful use of security-deposit money may be a disorderly-persons offense with a fine of at least $200 or imprisonment for not more than 30 days, or both.
rules.quoted_span:
The landlord may only require one and one -half times the tenant’s monthly rent as security and 
the first month’s rent at the inception of the lease.

rules.title: Prohibition on discriminatory rental screening and refusals
rules.requirement: A landlord or rental agency may not refuse to rent or discriminate in rentals based on protected traits including race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, nationality, or lawful source of income. A landlord may still refuse an applicant for stated nondiscriminatory reasons such as insufficient income, overcrowding, zoning-occupancy violations, or poor credit history.
rules.key_value: Protected classes include lawful source of income

coverage.other_unresolvable: Exceptions stated for rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home, residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex, and age-restricted housing as it pertains to familial status.
coverage.summary: Applies to landlord-tenant relationships except stated owner-occupied and other listed housing situations.

rules.exemptions: Two-family owner-occupied dwellings; rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home; residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex; and age-restricted housing as it pertains to familial status.
rules.penalty: Landlords who violate the LAD are subject to substantial fines and penalties, up to $10,000 for a first offense, and may be required to pay monetary damages and rent the unit to the complainant.
rules.interaction: The document also references federal fair-housing protections and complaint options, but the extracted rule is the New Jersey LAD rule.
rules.quoted_span:
The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), 
N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires 
equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin,

rules.law_name: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act rent-increase notice rule
rules.title: Rent increases require lease termination, notice, and must not be unconscionable
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot raise rent during the middle of a lease term; the old lease must be terminated and the landlord must offer a new lease with the increased rent. Before evicting for nonpayment of an increased rent, the owner must serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase, and the increase must not be unconscionable or violate municipal rent-control ordinances.
rules.key_value: No mid-lease increases; increase must not be unconscionable

coverage.summary: Applies to rent increases for tenants where the landlord seeks to terminate the current lease and continue the tenancy at a higher rent; the excerpt states no building-size cutoff.

rules.penalty: If an increase is unconscionable or proper notice was not given, the tenant may complain to a municipal rent control board where one exists; otherwise, a judge may decide the issue in an eviction action for nonpayment of the rent increase.
rules.interaction: The document states that rent increases must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord cannot raise the 
rent mid-lease term. The old lease must be terminated, and the new lease must have the increased 
rental payment.

rules.title: Thirty-year exemption from local rent control for newly constructed multiple dwellings
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent-control ordinances for 30 years after construction is completed. A tenant should check with the local rent-control board or municipal clerk to learn whether a unit is covered by local rent control.

coverage.summary: Applies to newly constructed multiple dwellings during the 30 years after completion of construction.

rules.interaction: The law exempts covered newly constructed multiple dwellings from municipal rent-control ordinances for the stated 30-year period.
rules.quoted_span:
Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly 
constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period 
of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.

rules.law_name: Condominium, cooperative, or fee-simple conversion rent-increase restriction
rules.title: No rent increase solely to cover conversion costs
rules.requirement: If a building is converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee-simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover costs that result solely from the conversion. The document states that this does not bar rent increases for new services or amenities.
rules.key_value: No increases for costs resulting solely from conversion

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies when a building is converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee-simple ownership of units.
coverage.summary: Covers tenants in buildings converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee-simple ownership of units, regardless of whether they are eligible for protected tenancy as seniors or disabled persons.

rules.exemptions: The document states this prohibition does not mean rents may not be increased to cover the cost of new services or amenities.
rules.interaction: The document states the prohibition applies to all tenants in the converted building regardless of protected-tenancy eligibility as senior citizens or disabled persons.
rules.quoted_span:
If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee 
simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the 
conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).
